review: The hymn is Hebrews 11:26 with 1 Peter 2:21 and 4:14: 1:1–4 is Matt 10:24–25 (אֵין תַּלְמִיד מֵעַל רַבּוֹ) with John 15:20, 2:1–4 Heb 12:2 with 1 Pet 2:21, and 3:1–4 is Heb 11:26 (חֶרְפַּת הַמָּשִׁיחַ … מֵאוֹצְרוֹת מִצְרַיִם) nearly verbatim.

3:3–4 כִּי חֶרְפַּת הַמָּשִׁיחַ / טוֹבָה מֵאוֹצְרוֹת זָהָב — the Arabic فَعَارُ الْمَسِيحِ أَفْضَل / مِنْ خَزَائِنِ الذَّهَب is Heb 11:26, but the verse says 'treasures of Egypt'; the Hebrew follows the Arabic's 'gold' because the hymn has generalised the contrast, and it keeps the comparative טוֹבָה rather than the verse's מֵאוֹצְרוֹת.

1:2 נִבְזָה — the Arabic أُهِين is 'was insulted'; the Hebrew uses בָּזָה, the verb of Isa 53:3 (נִבְזֶה וַחֲדַל אִישִׁים), so the Saviour's disgrace is the Servant's and the stanza's argument is that the servant cannot expect better treatment than the master.

2:4 אַחֲרֵי הַשֶּׂה — the Arabic وَرَا الْحَمَل is 'behind the Lamb'; the Hebrew keeps the singular שֶׂה, the same title as hymn 262, so the following is not a general discipleship but a walk behind the Sacrifice.

4:2 מִכָּל־מְקֻוֶּה אוֹ מְבֻקָּשׁ — the Arabic مِمَّا يُرْجَى أَوْ يُرَام is 'from whatever is hoped or sought'; Hebrew has no passive of קָוָה in the required sense, so the line uses the Pual participles, which keeps the two verbs distinct and lets the line stay short.
